title: Democrats Push Back on GOP Ethics Text as Thune Doubts a Pre-Recess Clarity Vote
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Democrats Push Back on GOP Ethics Text as Thune Doubts a Pre-Recess Clarity Vote
Senate Democrats have rejected the ethics provision in the latest Clarity Act draft in blunt terms, and Majority Leader John Thune cast doubt on Thursday that the crypto market-structure bill can pass ...
content:
Senate Democrats have rejected the ethics provision in the latest Clarity Act draft in blunt terms, and Majority Leader John Thune cast doubt on Thursday that the crypto market-structure bill can pass before the August recess.

“Whatever piece of s–t they sent back to us, that was not a serious effort,” Senator Ruben Gallego of Arizona told Politico, faulting Republicans for turning months of talks into language he called far from a deal. Gallego said he is at work on a counteroffer with Senator Thom Tillis of North Carolina “and other Republicans that are not being named right now.” “We are still in this fight,” he said. “We are going to send back language.”

The dispute centers on enforcement. Democrats say they will not accept an ethics provision with the Department of Justice as its sole enforcer, a stance rooted in distrust of the Trump Justice Department to police the president. 

Earlier talks broke down over the role state attorneys general would play in enforcing the rules.

The GOP language came from an agreement between the White House and Republican Senators Cynthia Lummis and Bernie Moreno. Lummis defended it, and said in a statement that “President Trump is supporting the most robust ethics rules ever imposed on the office of the presidency.” 

The new draft would bar federal officials from issuing digital assets and would sunset in 2029, and the White House has pressed Democrats to accept it. Tillis called the White House-approved language “good,” yet allowed that “the baseline… falls short of what some of the Democrats want,” and said one more talk with the White House lies ahead.

The ethics fight traces to President Trump’s crypto ventures, which a July disclosure tied to more than $1 billion in income over the past year. A group of seven Democrats led by Angela Alsobrooks said this week the text “falls short” on consumer protection, illicit finance, and conflicts of interest.

The Clarity Act has 14 days before the August deadline

Thune tempered expectations on the calendar. Industry and congressional negotiators had marked August 7 as the date the bill needed to clear the Senate for a real shot at passage this year. 

“I don’t think we’ll be able to get them done,” Thune told reporters, in reference to Clarity and a separate college-sports bill. “I would like to at least get Clarity started. We’ll see where the votes are.”

A start before the recess would leave the bill for a narrow window in September, with midterm campaigning and other priorities set to crowd the floor. Thune’s staff pointed to a Russia sanctions bill that the late Senator Lindsey Graham championed as the next item for floor time. White House crypto adviser Patrick Witt pushed back on Thune’s read, and told CoinDesk he was “perplexed” and “slightly more optimistic,” with the first week of August still open.

The bill has moved through months of bipartisan talks, and the House passed its version in July 2025. Beyond ethics, some Republicans have flagged the treatment of stablecoin yield, and Goldman Sachs, one of the bill’s backers, sits opposite JPMorgan in a Wall Street split over the measure. Galaxy Research has cut its passage odds to 50-50.

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

title: Saylor and team overhaul Strategy's bitcoin metrics as bear market persists
summary: New framework gives common shareholders a clearer view of net bitcoin exposure after preferred stock and convertible debt obligations
content:
Jul 24, 2026, 1:15 p.m.

2 min read

Summary

  • Strategy’s net reserve stands at $36.6 billion after subtracting $6.8 billion of out-of-the-money convertible debt and $15.5 billion of preferred stock from its bitcoin and cash reserves.
  • The revised mNAV permanently sets the equity issuance threshold at 1.0x, while a 3.22% BTC breakeven ARR would allow bitcoin gains to cover interest and preferred dividend obligations indefinitely.

Strategy (MSTR), the biggest corporate holder of bitcoin, has created a new market metrics framework, replacing gross BTC-based figures with net equivalents that take out the company's growing preferred stock and convertible debt obligations. The purpose of the new framework is to give common equity holders a more transparent overview of the company’s position.

The metric overhaul is part of a broader pattern, with Strategy repeatedly refining its guidance over the past year as it grapples with a bear market that began in October. The company’s flagship preferred stock, STRC, trades near $85 and has not returned to its intended $100 par value since mid-May.

Bitcoin is currently trading at roughly $65,000, 50% below its all-time high, while MSTR sits 84% below its November 2024 peak.

The first metric is the new "Net Reserve", which currently sits at $36.6 billion. That figure takes Strategy's $55.6 billion BTC reserve (843,775 BTC), adds $3.2 billion in USD reserves, then subtracts $6.8 billion in out-of-the-money convertible debt and $15.5 billion in notional preferred, the $22.3 billion in senior claims that rank ahead of common shareholders in any liquidation scenario.

The company has also updated its multiple to net asset value (mNAV) formula. Under the old accounting method, the accretion threshold would usually keep the company’s mNAV above 1.0x, making it increasingly difficult to know whether new share issuance was actually beneficial for existing holders. The new formula anchors that threshold permanently at 1.0x — if MSTR trades above it, issuing new shares adds BTC per share for all investors.

According to the company, the formula is: MSTR Price, divided by Net Bitcoin Per Share, representing whether MSTR trades above or below Net Bitcoin Per Share after debt and preferred claims.

The BTC Floor ARR is the minimum sustained BTC growth rate over the credit structure's duration before restructuring becomes a consideration for the company. Currently, the BTC Breakeven ARR sits at 3.22%, meaning bitcoin only needs to appreciate faster than that rate annually for Strategy to fund all interest and dividend obligations through BTC gains alone, in perpetuity.

Strategy has also introduced new bitcoin market metrics, such as the premium to the 200-week moving average and the Fear and Greed Index.

BTCC, the world’s longest-serving cryptocurrency exchange and an official regional sponsor of the Argentine Football Association (AFA), marked the close of its 15 Years in the Game: The BTCC World Cup Showdown on July 21, 2026. 

The campaign drew more than 80,000 participants and ran through every match of Argentina’s 2026 World Cup knockout journey, rewarding traders who timed their activity around the national team’s biggest games.

Campaign Trading Volume

Across the full campaign period, BTCC recorded a 22% increase in futures trading volume compared with pre-campaign levels. The gain traces directly to the platform’s 1.25x volume boost during the 24-hour window before each Argentina match kicked off. For traders, the boost gives them another opportunity to climb the weekly and overall leaderboards.

Group Stage

On June 15, 2026, ahead of Argentina’s match against Algeria, daily futures trading volume reached approximately $2.84 billion, about 15% above the average of surrounding days. Six days later, ahead of the Argentina vs. Austria match on June 21, volume climbed to approximately $2.35 billion, a 55% jump from the previous day.

Knockout Stage

BTCC’s 1.25x volume boost carried through all five of Argentina’s knockout matches, with three outperforming the campaign’s July daily average.

Best Brokers in Vietnam in 2026: IUX, Exness, and Pepperstone

Vietnam’s retail trading market continues to expand in 2026. Traders are still focused on spreads and execution speed, but account-entry clarity, regulatory transparency, mobile platform quality, and funding practicality now carry equal weight in broker selection.

For this comparison, we evaluate IUX, Exness, and Pepperstone, three of the best brokers for Vietnam in 2026, across the practical checks that matter most to Vietnam-based traders: regulation and entity visibility, leverage parameters, trading platforms, tradable asset coverage, account types, minimum deposit structure, fee clarity, and English/Vietnamese accessibility where available.

Risk Warning: Trading Contracts for Difference (CFDs) and other leveraged products carries a high risk to your capital. You may lose more than your initial deposit. Ensure you fully understand the risks involved before opening a live account. Leveraged trading is not suitable for all investors.

How We Selected the Best Brokers in Vietnam in 2026

This comparison is built around eight practical evaluation criteria applied consistently across all three brokers.

First, regulation and entity transparency: Users should be able to identify which legal entity serves their region and what regulator oversees it.

Second, maximum leverage: Leverage availability is a key consideration for Vietnam-based traders who are generally not subject to EU or UK retail leverage caps, depending on the onboarded entity.

Third, trading platforms: We assess what platforms are available and how well they support trading styles common among Vietnam retail users.

Fourth, tradable assets: We document the range of instrument categories each broker presents for retail access.

Fifth, account types: Named account tiers make it easier to select the right entry point without unnecessary onboarding friction.

Sixth, minimum deposit: Entry threshold visibility helps traders plan before funding.

Seventh, spreads and fees: Cost structure transparency is a core pre-funding evaluation step.

Eighth, Vietnam accessibility: Practical access, English-language readiness, mobile onboarding, support hours across Asian sessions, and funding routes relevant to Vietnam users, still affects day-to-day trader experience.

IUX Overview for Vietnam-Based Traders

IUX Features

IUX has built its brokerage model around speed, accessibility, and platform simplicity, targeting traders looking for a modern CFD trading experience without unnecessary complexity.

For traders in Vietnam, IUX positions itself as a broker focused on efficient market access, user-friendly trading platforms, and infrastructure capable of supporting active trading across global financial markets.

Regulation and Compliance

IUX operates through several international regulatory entities, including oversight from ASIC in Australia, the FSCA in South Africa, and the FSC in Mauritius, while also maintaining an offshore entity in Saint Vincent and the Grenadines.

For traders in Vietnam, accounts are typically serviced through IUX’s international entities rather than a Vietnam-based regulated entity. Vietnam currently does not maintain a domestic retail forex and CFD licensing framework for international brokers, meaning local traders commonly access global brokers through offshore regulated structures.

IUX also states that client funds are held in segregated accounts separate from company operational balances, alongside AML, KYC, and client fund protection procedures designed to support operational transparency and account security.

Trading Infrastructure and Execution Stability

Infrastructure reliability is one of the main areas where IUX focuses its offering. The broker promotes a low-latency STP execution environment supported by liquidity aggregation, direct routing technology, and enterprise-grade server protection systems.

Its infrastructure includes DDoS protection, traffic filtering systems, and direct cross-connectivity to liquidity providers designed to reduce downtime and improve execution consistency during volatile market sessions.

The broker provides access to more than 165 CFD instruments covering forex, commodities, stocks, indices, and crypto-related products through a single trading environment.

Platform Flexibility and Trading Experience

IUX combines proprietary trading tools with the established MetaTrader ecosystem. Traders can choose between the IUX App, IUX WebTerminal, and MT5 WebTrader.

The IUX App is designed for traders who prefer mobile-first trading access, with integrated portfolio tracking, chart management, and position monitoring features. Meanwhile, MT5 WebTrader continues to support traders looking for more traditional charting and order execution functionality..

This balanced platform structure allows IUX to appeal to both beginner traders and more experienced CFD users across Vietnam’s growing online trading community.

Education and Client Support

IUX promotes a trading environment that combines platform access with educational support and continuous customer assistance. The broker offers educational materials aimed at helping traders better understand CFD products, market movements, and trading strategies.

Alongside its learning resources, IUX provides 24/7 multilingual support designed to assist traders operating across different market sessions and regions. For newer traders entering the CFD market, this type of support structure can help improve usability and overall trading confidence.

Pros & Cons

Pros

Cons

Multi-regulated broker structure including ASIC oversight.

Institutional trading features remain limited.

Strong mobile trading accessibility through the IUX App.

The product ecosystem is still expanding globally.

STP execution model supported by deep liquidity connectivity.

24/7 multilingual support and educational resources.

Exness Overview for Vietnam-Based Traders

Exness Features

Exness has built a large Southeast Asian retail footprint by prioritising account accessibility, flexible funding rails, and MetaTrader familiarity. For Vietnam-based traders, the brand is often shortlisted when low entry barriers, frequent withdrawals, and multi-account pricing options matter as much as platform choice.

Rather than positioning itself as a niche proprietary-only broker, Exness operates as a high-volume multi-asset CFD broker with Standard and professional-style account tiers, broad instrument coverage, and a strong emphasis on deposit/withdrawal speed across supported payment methods.

Regulation and Compliance

Exness operates through a multi-entity group structure and cites licences from several authorities depending on entity, including the FCA (UK), CySEC (Cyprus), FSCA (South Africa), and offshore authorities such as the FSA (Seychelles) and FSC (Mauritius).

For traders in Vietnam, accounts are typically serviced through international Exness entities rather than a Vietnam-based regulated entity. As with other global brokers serving the market, local traders commonly access the brand through offshore regulated structures. Always confirm which legal entity appears in your client agreement and what client-fund protections apply to that entity.

Exness publicly emphasises segregated client funds and publishes regulation disclosures by entity. Protections and product terms can differ by the entity that accepts your account.

Trading Infrastructure and Execution Stability

Exness frames its trading offer around market execution across MetaTrader and its own Exness Terminal, with account types that separate spread-only pricing from raw/zero-style commission models. Vietnam-based traders typically weigh this against how consistently spreads hold during news events and whether their preferred instruments are available under the onboarded entity.

Instrument coverage generally includes forex pairs plus CFDs on metals, energies, indices, stocks, and cryptocurrencies, with the exact symbol list depending on account and region. The broker’s infrastructure pitch centres on stable order processing and flexible leverage settings by account type, leverage remains a major risk factor and should be treated as a risk amplifier, not a feature to maximise.

Where Exness often differentiates in Vietnam discussions is operational cash movement: support for low minimum deposits on entry-level accounts and a reputation for fast withdrawals on eligible methods when KYC is complete. Traders should still test a small deposit/withdrawal cycle before scaling size.

Platform Flexibility and Trading Experience

Exness supports MetaTrader 4, MetaTrader 5, and the proprietary Exness Terminal. This gives Vietnam-based traders a familiar MT4/MT5 workflow for EAs and indicators, plus a browser/app-style terminal for simpler monitoring and order management.

Account types typically include Standard and Standard Cent entry options alongside Pro / Raw Spread / Zero-style professional tiers. Entry-level minimums are commonly cited around the low tens of USD (or local-rail equivalents via supported methods), while professional tiers usually require higher minimums. Confirm live thresholds in the account opening flow for your payment method.

For traders who already know MetaTrader, Exness usually feels operationally familiar. For traders who want a more curated proprietary-first experience, IUX’s app/web stack may feel cleaner; for traders who want the broadest third-party platform choice, Pepperstone may be the stronger fit.

Education and Client Support

Exness provides help-centre guidance, platform documentation, and multi-channel support rather than positioning education as its primary brand differentiator. Support availability and language coverage can vary by region and contact channel.

Vietnam beginners often choose Exness for the low starting deposit and funding flexibility, then learn risk management elsewhere (demo trading, independent education, and strict position sizing). More experienced traders usually shortlist Exness when withdrawal speed and MT4/MT5 continuity are the priority.

Pros & Cons

Pros

Cons

Strong SEA retail presence with multi-jurisdiction group licences.

Multi-entity setup means protections and terms depend on your onboarded entity.

Low entry barriers on Standard/Cent-style accounts; strong funding/withdrawal focus.

Very high leverage availability on some accounts increases loss risk if misused.

MT4, MT5, and Exness Terminal cover both classic and proprietary workflows.

Broad CFD market coverage across forex and non-forex asset classes.

Pepperstone Overview for Vietnam-Based Traders

Pepperstone Features

Pepperstone is positioned as a platform-flexibility broker with strong execution branding and region-based legal segmentation. For Vietnam-based traders comparing professional toolsets, the multi-platform stack is one of Pepperstone’s clearest differentiators.

Compared with IUX’s leaner proprietary + MT5 setup and Exness’s low-friction funding narrative, Pepperstone sits closer to an execution-led multi-platform offer for traders who may outgrow a single app and want MetaTrader, cTrader, or TradingView in one brand.

Regulation and Compliance

Pepperstone is regulated by multiple authorities including the FCA, ASIC, CySEC, DFSA, SCB, BaFin, and CMA, depending on entity. Regulation and legal context are presented through region-specific website paths, allowing users to review terms based on their selected onboarding flow.

For traders in Vietnam, accounts are typically serviced through international Pepperstone entities rather than a Vietnam-based regulated entity. Local traders should verify which legal entity applies to their account and confirm that the chosen onboarding path matches their residency and risk expectations.

As with IUX and Exness, treat the published licence list as a starting point, then map it to the exact legal entity named in your client agreement before funding.

Trading Infrastructure and Execution Stability

Pepperstone’s retail positioning emphasises tight pricing and professional-style execution framing. Razor accounts are designed for traders who want raw spreads plus commission, while Standard accounts use spread-only pricing.

Product scope typically covers forex, indices, commodities, shares/CFDs, and crypto CFDs, with exact availability depending on entity and account. Vietnam-based traders who scalp, automate, or switch platforms often shortlist Pepperstone for pricing transparency and tool flexibility rather than for a single proprietary mobile experience.

Minimum deposit and leverage vary by entity. Traders should validate average spreads, commission, and stop-out rules on a demo or micro live size before committing significant margin.

Platform Flexibility and Trading Experience

Pepperstone supports MT4, MT5, cTrader, and TradingView. This broad platform coverage is useful for Vietnam traders who switch between discretionary, chart-intensive, and system-driven trading styles.

The English-language site and APAC-oriented infrastructure make Pepperstone operationally accessible for many Vietnam-based users, though Vietnamese-language depth can vary by page and support channel. Confirm live platform and funding options during onboarding.

Traders who want the widest third-party platform choice may prefer Pepperstone. Traders who want a simpler proprietary + MT5 stack may prefer IUX; traders who prioritise ultra-low entry and withdrawal speed often compare Pepperstone directly with Exness.

Education and Client Support

Pepperstone provides help-centre documentation, platform guidance, and multi-channel support. Education is available, but the brand’s strongest signal for many active traders remains platform choice and execution framing rather than beginner-course depth alone.

For newer Vietnam traders, Pepperstone can still work well if the priority is learning on MT4/MT5 or TradingView with clear Standard vs Razor pricing. Experienced traders should focus on entity terms, average spreads, and withdrawal reliability under the entity they join.

Pros & Cons

Pros

Cons

Broad multi-platform stack: MT4, MT5, cTrader, and TradingView.

Onboarding entity and conditions vary by region path.

Clear Standard vs Razor pricing structure for different trading styles.

Bitcoinist.App Brings Private Mining Pools to iOS
The only Bitcoin mining app on the Apple App Store that lets users create private pools, invite friends and family to combine hashpower, and compete with the global Bitcoin hashrate, while payouts go directly to wallets they control...
content:
RAS AL KHAIMAH, UAE, July 23, 2026: BFM Company Limited today introduced Bitcoinist.App, a non-custodial Bitcoin mining app and Learn-to-Mine platform released exclusively for iOS. Available from the Apple App Store, Bitcoinist.App gives people a simple way to learn how Bitcoin mining works, access real hashpower, create private Bitcoin mining pools, and receive payouts directly to a wallet they control. Onboarding uses Sign in with Apple, and users can begin from an iPhone without buying mining hardware or entering payment information.

Most people will never run a miner at home. In some regions, particularly parts of the developing world, high room temperatures can cause mining equipment to overheat, while the electricity needed to run air conditioning around the clock can make home mining prohibitively expensive. Noise and the miner’s own continuous power draw add to the barrier. In many parts of the world, people access the internet primarily through mobile data on a phone, without a practical wired connection for dedicated mining equipment. A physical miner also needs a stable network connection. Bitcoinist.App lowers those barriers with a simple iOS interface for learning about Bitcoin and directing real, remotely hosted hashpower through three modes:

  • Learn and unlock. The built-in Bitcoin Academy offers a 31-lesson video curriculum that explains Bitcoin and mining in practical terms. Educational videos and optional rewarded ads can unlock free mining rental time, so users can start mining from day one without a purchase.
  • Rent or connect. Paid access is offered through an in-app subscription. Users can access hashpower in 1 TH/s increments from miners hosted in UAE data centers and third-party facilities, or from capacity supplied through third-party hashpower marketplaces. Mining does not run on the iPhone. The app is a simple control layer for real hashpower, and pricing is published in the app. Support for connecting user-owned hardware, including home miners like the Bitaxe, is planned.
  • Route and pool. Users can create a private mining pool, invite friends and family to combine hashpower, and compete with the global hashrate. They can also mine solo or route miners to the Ocean pool for steadier payouts.

Bitcoinist.App is strictly non-custodial. There is no internal wallet or platform balance. Users choose an external self-custody wallet for payouts; mined bitcoin is sent to that address rather than held inside the app. Bitcoinist.App does not hold user private keys or mined funds.

Bitcoinist.App provides mining infrastructure and education, not a yield product, investment scheme, or custodial wallet. An in-app subscription or ad-supported access provides mining time, not bitcoin and not a promised return. Mining outcomes depend on network difficulty, pool performance, transaction fees, and deployed hashpower. Some hosting and hashpower capacity comes from third parties, so availability and performance can vary by provider. Nothing in this release guarantees any amount of mined bitcoin.

“We designed Bitcoinist.App to orange pill the masses through mining and education,” said Fouad Jamil, Founder and CEO of Bitcoinist.App. “People can begin with a phone, learn what Bitcoin mining actually does, direct real hashpower, and receive every sat in a wallet they control. We are not mining for users and we never custody their bitcoin. We provide the infrastructure and tools; users decide where their hashpower goes.”

Bitcoinist.App is operated by BFM Company Limited, registered in RAK DAO, Ras Al Khaimah, UAE (Bitcoin Mining license No. 07010714), with mining infrastructure in UAE data centers and third-party mining facilities around the world. Additional capacity may be supplied through third-party hashpower marketplaces. Availability is subject to regional eligibility.

Download the app

Bitcoinist.App is now publicly available exclusively on iOS. Users can download the app from the Apple App Store.

Designed for ease of use, it lets people learn about Bitcoin, unlock free mining rental time through educational videos and optional rewarded ads, or choose an in-app subscription for ongoing access to real hashpower. Users can create private mining pools with friends and family, compete with the global Bitcoin hashrate, or route miners to Ocean, while payouts go directly to self-custody. Coinbase is taking action to prepare Bitcoin for the challenges of next-generation cybersecurity, introducing a new industry alliance to help protect the network from quantum computing attacks: The Bitcoin Security Consortium.

The consortium comprises industry giants in the financial sector and the Bitcoin industry to help coordinate research, engineering and public education efforts on Bitcoin’s long-term cryptographic security.

Industry Leaders Unite Around Bitcoin Security

Coinbase has revealed it is setting up the Bitcoin Security Consortium alongside firms alongside BlackRock, Fidelity Digital Assets, Block, Blockstream, Strategy, and others in the crypto ecosystem.

We’re proud to announce the launch of the Bitcoin Security Consortium, in partnership with BlackRock, Fidelity, Block, and more.

Together we’ll support the long-term security of the Bitcoin network.

Quantum computing is coming. Crypto needs to be ready. pic.twitter.com/T792xvP7jj

— Coinbase 🛡️ (@coinbase) July 23, 2026

The initiative is meant to make Bitcoin more resilient and protect it from being outcompeted by quantum computers, which are one possible enemy. Although experts believe it’s still years away, Coinbase feels prepared now is the time because upgrades to decentralized networks are costly and time consuming.

Engineering Support Goes Beyond Funding

Coinbase will provide engineering resources directly to open-source Bitcoin development and also give to quantum-resistant progress endeavors.

It provides proposals, technical work and support to Bitcoin’s transition to post-quantum cryptography like BIP-360.

Coinbase Builds Quantum-Ready Infrastructure

Alongside the consortium launch, Coinbase revealed it is developing PQ-CoreKMS, a post-quantum version of its proprietary key management system.

The company currently provides CoreKMS with multi-party computation technology (MPC), which helps it achieve approximately 99.9% of its assets in custody. New signature schemes that are quantum-safe would be generated using these technologies and secure enclaves on the upgraded platform.

Coinbase also pledged it would conduct an audit of cryptographic systems used in all of its operations to determine priorities for migration and set technical milestones for broader migration once quantum technology becomes capable of certain major abilities.

Developers Begin Coordinating Bitcoin’s Next Upgrade

Getting agreement throughout its decentralized ecosystem is the way to prepare Bitcoin for post quantum security, not one firm’s.

Stanford Workshop Kicks Off Collaborative Effort

In August, Coinbase will be holding a technical workshop in conjunction with Stanford University, to encourage industry cooperation. The exchange said the workshop was the first in a series that will focus on real engineering considerations, and not speculation.

This will be the day of quantum computing and change digital security over the Internet, including in blockchain networks, said Coinbase. The company says it will use internal infrastructure improvements and open-source collaboration through the Bitcoin Security Consortium to assist the Bitcoin ecosystem in preparing long in advance for quantum computing to become a real threat to security.

Key Takeaways:

  • On 23rd September, 2026, BitMEX will officially end its operations after conducting a strategic business review.
  • People are encouraged to close positions and withdraw funds, and exchange says all customer funds are safe.
  • The shutdown marks the end of one of crypto’s most influential trading platforms and the creator of the 100x perpetual swap.

BitMEX, one of the most iconic names in crypto derivatives trading, has announced that it will permanently shut down its exchange on September 23, 2026. After evaluating the company, the parent, HDR Global Trading, made that decision, which has ended over 10 years of service.

Dear BitMEX Users,

Today, we share with a very heavy heart that BitMEX exchange will shut down its operations, effective 23 September 2026 at 04:00:00 UTC.

The owner and operator of BitMEX, HDR Global Trading Limited, has made the difficult decision to close operations… pic.twitter.com/oWuqlh547f

BitMEX Confirms Exchange Closure

BitMEX announced that trading will cease at 04:00 UTC on September 23 for users in a statement to them. This platform has already suspended new account registrations and is encouraging its customers to start withdrawing as early as possible.

The exchange stressed that user assets remain fully backed and under customer control throughout the transition period. The company says the early announcement was meant as a precaution for traders to close out any trades and transfer the capital before the situation becomes chaotic.

Also highlighting its security record is BitMEX, which states that there have never been any customer’s funds stolen by a hack in its entire life.

The Exchange That Changed Crypto Trading

The BitMEX exchange was launched in 2014 and gained significant influence in digital asset markets following the launch of the perpetual swap contracts offered with up to 100x leverage.

A Product That Became an Industry Standard

Perpetual futures quickly became the major commodity in crypto derivative trading and were later embraced by most of the crypto exchanges. Originally a BitMEX product that was intended for a specific few, it has since become the most actively traded digital asset on the exchange.

In its heyday, BitMEX had been one of the top choices for skilled traders looking to enter the gold trades with high leverage and liquidity. The platform helped popularize trading in cryptocurrencies among retail and institutional users and contributed to the formation of the trading landscape as it exists today.

Competition and Industry Changes Take Their Toll

BitMEX contributed to the establishment of the perpetual futures market, but competition gradually grew through the years, as bigger exchanges introduced derivative volumes. Rivals lured in liquidity through offering a variety of products, increasing user base, and ever more aggressive growth tactics.

Over the last decade, the exchange also faced a string of regulators’ issues. Several of the founders have left since legal issues involving anti-money laundering compliance (AML) have since arisen but operations have continued.

Those difficulties did not deter BitMEX, however, as they were still a familiar brand in the crypto space, and they didn’t alienate any traders.
